findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored, which breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.' With no surrogate, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type). That method takes every public read-write member, sorted by name, under a string key. It never checks [MessagePackObject], [Key] or [IgnoreMember] on T. As a result, a T from a referenced assembly declared as [MessagePackObject] { [Key(0)] Id; [IgnoreMember] SecretValue } gets a string-keyed map that includes SecretValue. Those bytes differ from what the dynamic resolver, or T's own generated formatter, produces.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.AttributedDataTypeFromReferencedAssembly_IgnoreMemberIsHonoured. It compiles ProjectA with [MessagePackObject]/[Key(0)]/[IgnoreMember], references it as metadata from ProjectB, runs MessagePackGenerator and asserts the generated MyTypeFormatter does not mention 'SecretValue'. It fails on head.

findings.claim: MsgPack020's message says the formatter must implement IMessagePackFormatter<T> 'for exactly one data type', but the code only rejects Length == 0. A formatter declared as `partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<A>, IMessagePackFormatter<B>` silently uses formatterInterfaces[0] and generates only that implementation. MsgPack020 is never reported; the user gets CS0535 for the missing IMessagePackFormatter<B> members instead.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.FormatterImplementingTwoDataTypes_ReportsMsgPack020. It expects a MsgPack020 diagnostic in GeneratorDriverRunResult.Diagnostics and fails on head.

findings.claim: The formatter's own accessibility is never validated: only partial-ness and the data type's accessibility are checked. A [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] declared as a private or protected nested class (e.g. `class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] private partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`) is still added to the resolver's ObjectInfos. The generated resolver then instantiates the inaccessible type, giving CS0122 in generated code instead of a MessagePack diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Collect checks IsPartial and IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter), but never compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(formatter, resolver/assembly). Confirm with a test that declares a private nested generated formatter plus a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] and inspects the output compilation for CS0122.

findings.claim: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>` is silently dropped. AttributeTargets.Class allows the attribute on a record class, but the ForAttributeWithMetadataName predicate only accepts ClassDeclarationSyntax (RecordDeclarationSyntax is a different node). So no formatter is generated and no MsgPack019/020 diagnostic is reported; the user sees only CS0535 for the unimplemented interface.

receipt_plan.detail: predicate: static (node, _) => node is ClassDeclarationSyntax excludes RecordDeclarationSyntax, and IsPartial also uses OfType<ClassDeclarationSyntax>(). Confirm with a generator test that declares a partial record formatter and asserts either generated output or a MsgPack diagnostic.

findings.claim: Surrogate mode enumerates every instance field and property of the surrogate and its base types, including private and protected ones. Any of those without [Key] or [IgnoreMember] aborts generation with MsgPack004. A surrogate with an ordinary private helper field (e.g. `private int cache;`) is therefore rejected, although MsgPack004 elsewhere only applies to public members and the attribute docs say only KeyAttribute-carrying members define the contract.

receipt_plan.detail: CreateSurrogateMembers loops over GetInstanceMembers(surrogate), which applies no accessibility filter, and returns null with MemberNeedsKey when key is not int/string. Confirm with a generator test whose surrogate has a private unkeyed field, asserting that no MsgPack004 is reported and the formatter is generated.
